key_findings: Fentanyl withdrawal (0.4 mg/kg/day minipump, 48 h) produces dose- and time-dependent mechanical hyperalgesia in mice.
Whole-brain Fos network analysis identifies the PAG as the central hub of the fentanyl withdrawal network.
Fentanyl withdrawal increases Fos expression in vlPAG neurons, including GAD67+ GABAergic neurons, and enhances inhibitory synaptic transmission (CRACM IPSCs).
Chemogenetic (hM4Di/CNO) inhibition of GABAergic vlPAG neurons reverses withdrawal-induced mechanical hyperalgesia.
Inhibiting GABAergic vlPAG neurons prevents escalation of fentanyl self-administration in males but not females.
